A 500-Calorie Daily Deficit: What to Eat, Dish by Dish

A 500-calorie daily deficit is about 0.45 kg a week. This is what it looks like on the table: two real days of eating in Spain, for a woman and a man, with every dish and its figure.

November 5, 2026 · By Fotocal, Madrid · 5 min read

Part 4 of 12 in Calories, from the ground up

This is not medical advice

If you are pregnant, living with diabetes or another condition, taking medication, under eighteen, or have any history of an eating disorder, please speak to a doctor or a registered dietitian before changing how you eat or using a calorie tracker. Their advice comes first, and nothing here overrides it.

"500-calorie deficit a day" is one of the most searched phrases when people start a diet, and almost everything that comes up explains the maths but not the plate. Here is the plate. Two full days of normal eating in Spain, one for a woman and one for a man, with each item in its portion as it is served and its figure from the calorie table for Spanish dishes, the same database the app uses. First of all, your own figure: the calorie deficit calculator gives you your expenditure and your target in a minute, without signing up.

What a 500-calorie deficit means

Eating 500 calories fewer than you burn each day. Over a week that's 3,500, and with the usual approximation of 7,700 kcal per kilo of fat, about 0.45 kg a week. It isn't exact, because the body burns a little less as it weighs less, but it gives you the order of magnitude: about two kilos a month at first, somewhat less later on.

The two days below use the examples from the daily calorie calculator: a woman with an expenditure of 2,130 kcal and a man at 2,780. With 500 less, their targets are 1,630 and 2,280 kcal. For her the cut is 23% of her expenditure; for him, 18%. Both fall within the moderate range (between 15% and 25%) explained in the article on the calorie deficit.

A day at 1,630 kcal (woman, expenditure of 2,130)

  • Breakfast: café con leche (coffee with milk), 200 ml, 91 kcal, and tostada con tomate y aceite (toast with tomato and oil), 90 g, 235 kcal.
  • Mid-morning: a banana, 120 g, 107 kcal.
  • Lunch: lentejas estofadas (stewed lentils), 320 g, 373 kcal; a piece of bread, 50 g, 133 kcal; an orange, 180 g, 65 kcal.
  • Afternoon snack: a high-protein yoghurt, 160 g, 100 kcal.
  • Dinner: baked hake with vegetables, 250 g, 272 kcal, and cream of courgette soup, 300 g, 158 kcal.
  • After dinner: an apple, 150 g, 78 kcal.

Total: 1,612 kcal and about 87 g of protein. That's five meals, and none of them is "diet food": lentils at lunchtime, fish in the evening, bread with lunch. What makes the day add up is what isn't there: no second piece of bread, no sweet dessert, no drink with calories.

A day at 2,280 kcal (man, expenditure of 2,780)

  • Breakfast: café con leche, 91 kcal; tostada con tomate y aceite, 235 kcal; a two-egg tortilla francesa (plain omelette), 100 g, 190 kcal.
  • Mid-morning: a banana, 107 kcal.
  • Lunch: garbanzos con espinacas (chickpeas with spinach), 320 g, 413 kcal; grilled chicken breast, 150 g, 175 kcal; a piece of bread, 133 kcal; an orange, 65 kcal.
  • Afternoon snack: Greek yoghurt with honey, 150 g, 182 kcal, and an apple, 78 kcal.
  • Dinner: grilled cuttlefish, 180 g, 170 kcal; mixed salad, 250 g, 210 kcal; a piece of bread, 133 kcal; a caña (small draught beer), 86 kcal.

Total: 2,268 kcal and about 141 g of protein. There's room for a caña with dinner and two pieces of bread a day. A 500 deficit doesn't force you to give up anything in particular; it forces you to know how much each thing adds up to.

Where a 500-calorie deficit breaks down

On a day like these, 500 kcal is very little margin. Any one of these is enough to wipe it out entirely:

  • The oil that doesn't get logged. A tablespoon is 80 kcal; a frying pan gets two or three. Three unlogged tablespoons are half the deficit.
  • The Friday menú del día (set lunch). A menú with ensaladilla (Russian salad), calamares (battered squid), wine and arroz con leche (rice pudding) is 1,073 kcal; the light one, 518. Between the two lies a whole day's deficit.
  • The afternoon cañas. Three cañas and four shared tapas add up to about 926 kcal before dinner.
  • The weekend. Five days at a 500 deficit and two at 1,000 over leave the week at 500 in total, not 3,500. The scales don't move, and it looks as if the diet isn't working.

When 500 calories is too much

If your daily expenditure is low, 500 kcal can be too big a cut. With an expenditure of 1,700 kcal, taking off 500 leaves 1,200: 29% less, the floor that the calculator sets as the minimum for a woman, and above the moderate range. In that case a deficit of 300 to 400 kcal is better: lose weight more slowly and don't go hungry. The calculator warns you when your target falls below that floor or below your basal metabolic rate.

Conversely, with a high expenditure (3,000 kcal or more), 500 kcal is less than 17% and can be sustained without noticing. What isn't advisable is going beyond 25% for months: you lose muscle, hunger rises and the weight tends to come back, as the article on how much weight you can lose in a week explains.

How to keep count without weighing anything

The two days above can be logged in under two minutes if each dish already has its portion. Home and bar portions are fairly consistent (a plate of pulses, 320 g; a fillet, 150 g; a piece of bread, 50 g) and the app has them at that weight. A photo of the plate gives you the calories and macros; the bread, fruit and drink are added by hand. The free plan includes 2 AI scans and 1 voice log a day; the barcode scanner and Coach Kal are unlimited, and no card is required.

Key takeaways

  • A daily deficit of 500 kcal is about 0.45 kg a week, using the approximation of 7,700 kcal per kilo.
  • With ordinary Spanish dishes, 1,630 kcal (woman) and 2,280 kcal (man) are enough for five meals, bread, fruit and even a caña.
  • What breaks the deficit is what doesn't get logged: oil, drinks, the Friday menú and the weekend.
  • If your expenditure is low, 500 kcal may be too much: the calculator tells you where your floor is.

Questions people ask

How much weight do you lose with a 500-calorie daily deficit?

About 0.45 kg a week, using the approximation of 7,700 kcal per kilo of fat: 500 × 7 = 3,500 kcal a week. At first the scales drop a little more because of water, and over the months a little less, because the body burns less as it weighs less.

Is a 500-calorie daily deficit a lot?

It depends on how much you burn. With an expenditure of 2,000 to 2,800 kcal it's 18–25%, a moderate cut. With an expenditure of 1,700 kcal it's 29% and leaves you at 1,200, the sensible minimum for a woman: in that case a deficit of 300 to 400 is better.

What can I eat on a 500-calorie deficit?

Normal food in normal portions: pulses or rice at lunchtime, grilled fish or meat, vegetables, fruit, bread with one meal and even a caña. What you need to watch is what you don't see: oil, drinks with calories, snacking and the weekend.

This article is general information, not medical advice.
